---
title: "Causal inference with synthetic controls"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4)
```

A normalised series removes the weather, but an intervention such as a
low-emission zone still has to be separated from everything else that changed
at the same time. Synthetic control methods (SCM) build a counterfactual for
the treated site from a weighted combination of untreated "donor" sites.
normet provides several SCM variants, significance tests and diagnostics.

The chunks in this article run when the site is built, except ML-SCM, which
needs a modelling backend.

## Setup

The bundled `scm` dataset is a monthly panel of observed and normalised
(`NO2_dw`) NO2 for 104 UK monitoring sites (2016–2021). The question is the
effect of the London Ultra Low Emission Zone (ULEZ, launched 2019-04-08) at
Marylebone Road (`MY1`). Following the design of the
[Getting started](normet.html) vignette, take the pre-COVID window, use
traffic sites as the donor pool, and keep donors with complete coverage:

```{r}
library(normet)

win <- scm[scm$date >= as.Date("2017-01-01") & scm$date < as.Date("2020-03-01"), ]
traffic <- win[grepl("Traffic", win$type), ]
n_months <- length(unique(traffic$date))
coverage <- tapply(!is.na(traffic$NO2_dw), traffic$code, sum)
panel <- traffic[traffic$code %in% names(coverage)[coverage == n_months], ]

treated <- "MY1"
donors  <- setdiff(unique(panel$code), treated)
cutoff  <- "2019-04-01"
length(donors)
```

## SCM variants

`nm_run_scm()` is the common interface. `scm_backend = "scm"` is the augmented
SCM (`nm_scm()`), and `"mlscm"` is the machine-learning variant (`nm_mlscm()`).
The other estimators have their own functions with the same core arguments.

```{r}
scm_res <- nm_run_scm(
  df = panel, date_col = "date", unit_col = "code", outcome_col = "NO2_dw",
  treated_unit = treated, donors = donors, cutoff_date = cutoff,
  scm_backend = "scm", verbose = FALSE
)
head(scm_res)
nm_plot_time_series(scm_res, target = "effect", title = "ULEZ effect on normalised NO2 at MY1")
```

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# ML-SCM: exploratory only, not recommended for inference (see ?nm_mlscm).
# It trains a model, so it needs the lightgbm (default) or h2o backend.
ml_res <- nm_run_scm(
  df = panel, date_col = "date", unit_col = "code", outcome_col = "NO2_dw",
  treated_unit = treated, donors = donors, cutoff_date = cutoff,
  scm_backend = "mlscm"
)
```

```{r}
# Abadie (2010) quadratic-programme weights
ab_res <- nm_scm_abadie(
  df = panel, date_col = "date", unit_col = "code", outcome_col = "NO2_dw",
  treated_unit = treated, donors = donors, cutoff_date = cutoff
)

# Difference-in-differences baseline
did_res <- nm_did_baseline(
  df = panel, date_col = "date", unit_col = "code", outcome_col = "NO2_dw",
  treated_unit = treated, donors = donors, cutoff_date = cutoff
)

# Matrix-completion nuclear-norm minimisation
mc_res <- nm_scm_mcnnm(
  df = panel, date_col = "date", unit_col = "code", outcome_col = "NO2_dw",
  treated_unit = treated, donors = donors, cutoff_date = cutoff
)

# Robust SCM: HSVT de-noising (Amjad, Shah & Shen 2018)
rb_res <- nm_scm_robust(
  df = panel, date_col = "date", unit_col = "code", outcome_col = "NO2_dw",
  treated_unit = treated, donors = donors, cutoff_date = cutoff, verbose = FALSE
)

# Bayesian SCM (Dirichlet prior + Metropolis-Hastings)
bayes_res <- nm_bayesian_scm(
  df = panel, date_col = "date", unit_col = "code", outcome_col = "NO2_dw",
  treated_unit = treated, donors = donors, cutoff_date = cutoff,
  draws = 2000, ci_level = 0.95, verbose = FALSE
)
nm_plot_bayesian_scm(bayes_res, cutoff_date = cutoff)
```

For several treated units, each with its own cutoff, see
`nm_run_scm_staggered()`. `nm_scm_all()` fits every unit in turn.

## Significance tests

```{r, warning = FALSE}
# Conformal prediction interval on the average treatment effect
ci <- nm_conformal_effect_interval(scm_res, cutoff_date = cutoff, ci_level = 0.95)
str(ci)

# Placebo in space: refit with every donor as the "treated" unit
placebo <- nm_placebo_in_space(
  df = panel, date_col = "date", unit_col = "code", outcome_col = "NO2_dw",
  treated_unit = treated, donors = donors, cutoff_date = cutoff,
  scm_backend = "scm", verbose = FALSE
)
# RMSPE ratio test on the placebo distribution
rmspe <- nm_rmspe_ratio_test(placebo, cutoff_date = cutoff)
rmspe$p_value
```

`nm_placebo_in_time()` is a historical falsification test. It moves the cutoff
back into the pre-period, where there should be no effect. `min_pre_period` and
`placebo_every` count observations: months, for this panel.

```{r, warning = FALSE}
tp <- nm_placebo_in_time(
  df = panel, date_col = "date", unit_col = "code", outcome_col = "NO2_dw",
  treated_unit = treated, donors = donors, cutoff_date = cutoff,
  scm_backend = "scm", min_pre_period = 12, placebo_every = 1, verbose = FALSE
)
tp$p_value
```

`nm_pre_trend_test()` checks the pre-period for a trend in the gap between the
treated unit and its synthetic control.

## Effect bands and diagnostics

```{r}
# Bands from the placebo-in-space distribution
bands <- nm_effect_bands_space(placebo, level = 0.95, method = "quantile", verbose = FALSE)
nm_plot_effect_with_bands(bands, cutoff_date = cutoff)

# Jackknife (or bootstrap) uncertainty over the donor pool
jack <- nm_uncertainty_bands(
  df = panel, date_col = "date", unit_col = "code", outcome_col = "NO2_dw",
  treated_unit = treated, donors = donors, cutoff_date = cutoff,
  scm_backend = "scm", method = "jackknife", verbose = FALSE
)
nm_plot_uncertainty_bands(jack, cutoff_date = cutoff)
```

```{r, results = "hide"}
# Weight diagnostics, and how stable the weights are when each donor is left out
diag <- nm_scm_diagnostics(scm_res, cutoff_date = cutoff)
loo <- nm_loo_weight_stability(
  df = panel, date_col = "date", unit_col = "code", outcome_col = "NO2_dw",
  treated_unit = treated, donors = donors, cutoff_date = cutoff
)
```

`nm_plot_scm_dashboard()` draws the fit, the effect and (optionally) the
diagnostics on one figure.
